home.lead: Correct a few words in the PDF, or turn it into a Word or Pages document. It’s free, there’s nothing to sign up for, and your documents stay on your computer.

home.shot1_alt: Step 1 of PDF Edit, in French: the screen “Quel PDF voulez-vous modifier ?” (Which PDF do you want to edit?), with a large “Choisir un PDF…” (Choose a PDF…) button and an area to drop the file on.
home.shot2_alt: Step 2, in French: the screen “Que voulez-vous faire ?” (What do you want to do?) for the file “Lettre de l’association.pdf”, with three choices: correct a few words, edit in Pages, edit in Word.
home.shot3_alt: Step 3, in French: the screen “Où enregistrer le nouveau fichier ?” (Where should the new file be saved?), with three choices: on the Desktop, in Downloads, or in a folder you choose.

home.step1_caption: 1. Choose the PDF you want to edit.
home.step2_label: Step 2: what do you want to do?
home.step2_caption: 2. Correct a few words, or open it in Pages or Word.

home.correct_text: Click the line, type your correction, then press Return. It is written in the PDF’s own font, and the rest of the page stays exactly as it was.
home.correct_alt: A letter open in PDF Edit, in French: the date “Paris, le 10 novembre 2026” has just been retyped in the letter’s font and is outlined; at the bottom, “1 ligne modifiée” (1 line changed) and the button “Enregistrer sur le Bureau” (Save to Desktop).

faq.title: Frequently asked questions about PDF Edit
faq.description: Is it free? Are your documents sent anywhere? Do you need Word or Pages? Which macOS? Simple answers to common questions about PDF Edit.
faq.lead: What people often wonder before installing PDF Edit.
faq.1.a: Yes. You can edit a PDF for free and without signing up: the Mac app and the online version are free, with no ads and no subscription.
faq.2.q: Are my documents sent over the Internet?
faq.2.a: No. Your PDFs are read and converted on your computer, never sent. The only exception: if a free font is missing, the app downloads it once from Google Fonts; only the name of the font is requested, never the document.
faq.3.q: Do I need Word or Pages?
faq.3.a: To correct a few words directly in the PDF, no: you need nothing else. For “Modifier dans Pages” (Edit in Pages), Apple’s Pages app must be installed on the Mac. The Word file (.docx) opens in Word, and in Pages too.
faq.4.q: Which version of macOS do I need?
faq.4.a: macOS 11 Big Sur or later, on a Mac with an Intel processor as well as on an Apple Silicon Mac (M1 chips and later).
faq.5.a: The app is for the Mac only, but the online version also works on Windows and Linux, in a recent browser (Chrome, Edge or Firefox). It gives you a Word file (.docx).
faq.6.q: My PDF is protected by a password: will it work?
faq.6.a: Yes, to turn it into Word or Pages: PDF Edit asks you for the password, which stays on your computer. However, a protected PDF cannot be corrected directly yet.
faq.7.a: No. PDF Edit always creates a new file, in the place you choose: on the Desktop, in Downloads or in another folder. Your original PDF stays as it is, and no existing file is ever replaced.
faq.8.q: How do I uninstall PDF Edit?
faq.8.a: Open the Applications folder and drag PDF Edit (formerly “Modifier mes PDF”) to the Trash. Any free fonts it added stay on the Mac; you can remove them with the Font Book app.
privacy.title: Privacy and legal notice — PDF Edit
privacy.description: Who publishes PDF Edit, who hosts it and what the site measures: visits counted without cookies or IP addresses, and your documents never sent.
privacy.og_description: Who publishes PDF Edit, who hosts it, and what the site measures: visits counted without cookies, and your documents never sent.
privacy.lead: In short: your documents never leave your computer, the site sets no cookies, and it only counts its visits as anonymous totals.
privacy.publisher.p1: This site and the PDF Edit app are published by Makio. PDF Edit is free: nothing is sold, and there is no subscription and no advertising.
privacy.publisher.contact: For any question or comment, you can write on the project’s page: {{GITHUB_URL}}.
privacy.hosting.p1: The site is hosted by Netlify, Inc., 101 2nd Street, San Francisco, CA 94105, United States — netlify.com.
privacy.documents.p1: The Mac app reads and converts your PDFs on your Mac. The online version does the same, right in your browser: the PDF is processed on your computer.
privacy.documents.li1: No document, file name or content is sent to a server or kept by this site.
privacy.documents.li2: The password of a protected PDF is only used to open it, on your computer.
privacy.documents.li3: The new file is saved where you choose; your original PDF is not changed.
privacy.audience.p1: To know whether the site is useful, it counts its visits and downloads. The site does this itself, with no outside service, and with nothing that could identify you.
privacy.never.li1: No cookies, and no identifier kept in your browser.
privacy.never.li2: No IP address recorded, no fingerprint of your device.
privacy.never.li3: Nothing about your documents: no file name, no size, no content.
privacy.never.banner: That is why this site shows no cookie banner.
privacy.counted.pv: A page view: the page (home, online version, questions, privacy or page not found) and its language, whether you came from another site and, if so, which one (for example “google”, or only the site’s name, never the full address of the page), the campaign label utm_source if the link has one, the type of screen (phone or computer, from its width) and the type of system (Mac, iPhone or iPad, Windows, Android, Linux, ChromeOS or other).
privacy.counted.dl: A download of the Mac app, counted by the server when you click: the version, the button used (at the top of the page, at the bottom…), the language of the page and the type of system.
privacy.counted.online: In the online version: a conversion, finished or not, the format chosen (Pages or Word), its approximate duration (under 5 seconds, 5 to 15 seconds, and so on), a password request when one appears, and the opening or saving of a corrected PDF, successful or not.
privacy.counted.gh: A click to the source code page, with where the link was.
privacy.stored.p1: Each event is recorded as a simple counting line, with no identifier: the day, the type of event and the information above, with a technical mark (the moment it was recorded and a random number) that only serves to keep two lines apart. These lines are only read to make totals (per day, per page, per source…), and the totals of each past day are kept to follow how the site is doing. Only the publisher looks at these totals, on a private page.
privacy.optout.h3: If you do not want to be counted
privacy.optout.p1: One click on the button below is enough: this browser is no longer counted at all, neither for page views nor for downloads. The choice is kept in this browser as a simple setting (“do not count”), with no identifier. It applies to this browser only: on another computer or in another browser, you need to click again.
privacy.optout.status_off: This browser is no longer counted.
privacy.optout.status_signal: Your browser already asks not to be tracked: nothing is counted.
privacy.optout.status_blocked: This browser does not let this choice be saved. Its “Do Not Track” or Global Privacy Control setting still works.
privacy.optout.status_failed: The choice could not be saved in this browser.
privacy.optout.status_done_off: Done: this browser is no longer counted.
privacy.optout.status_done_on: Noted: this browser is counted again, anonymously.
privacy.optout.signals: Nothing is counted either if your browser sends the Global Privacy Control or “Do Not Track” signal: the site then sends nothing, and the server does not count downloads. Automated browsers and known robots are not counted.
privacy.logs.p1: Like any host, Netlify receives visitors’ IP addresses in order to send them the pages, protect the site against abuse (for example by limiting the number of requests) and keep technical logs. Netlify is responsible for this processing, under its privacy policy. This site’s statistics do not record these addresses.
privacy.fonts.p1: To reproduce a document faithfully, PDF Edit sometimes needs a free font that is missing on your computer (for example Carlito, which stands in for Calibri).
privacy.fonts.li1: The Mac app downloads it only once, from Google Fonts, then installs it on the Mac so that Pages and Word show the document correctly.
privacy.fonts.li2: The online version may ask a public font service for it (Fontsource, served by jsDelivr).
privacy.fonts.p2: In both cases, only the name of the font is requested, never the document. As with any connection, these services see the computer’s IP address. This site itself loads no outside fonts.
privacy.license.p1: The PDF Edit app is free. The texts and images of this site are © 2026 Makio.
privacy.license.code: The code of PDF Edit is open source, published under the MIT or Apache 2.0 license, whichever you prefer: see the source code.
